claim: A sweep with non-primitive keys re-enters the same item on every move
holdsFixed treats `will-change: contents` as making a box the containing block for fixed descendants, though it does not

triage.scenario: the `will-change` test is `/transform|translate|rotate|scale|perspective|filter|contain/`, and `contain` also matches the value `contents`, which does not create a containing block. Take a `position: fixed` rectEl (say, a fixed HUD with handles) with an ancestor marked `will-change: contents`. `scrollersOf` takes that ancestor as the fixed box's containing block and walks on up from it, adding the page's and other ancestors' scroll offsets. A scroll during the drag then shifts `localOf`'s box although the fixed element never moved. It should match `contain` as a whole word only, e.g. `/(^|,\s*)contain(\s*,|$)/` or a token split.
triage.cause: substring regex on a keyword list

claim: Sweep can't find items slotted into the surface

triage.scenario: (a) the surface is a custom element whose items live in its own shadow root → `elementAt(surface)` hit-tests in the surface's root (the document), gets back the surface itself (retargeted), and the loop `el !== surface` exits at once → null, so nothing sweeps. (b) the surface is inside a shadow root and its items are slotted light-DOM children → `surface.contains(el)` is false → null. In both cases `enabled` answers NotApplicable for every press. The walk up `parentElement` also stops at a shadow-root boundary instead of following the flat tree.
triage.cause: non-composed contains/parentElement in hit walk

claim: A carry's onMove still reaches the source after the carry was canceled from inside that same move

triage.scenario: a surface's `receive('enter' | 'move')` (a carry binding's action) or anything it triggers calls the carry's `cancel()` during `step(e)`. The session aborts, `onCancel` fires the leave and the source's `cb.onCancel`, then control returns to `onMove`, which still calls `cb.onMove?.(e)`: the source hears a move after its cancel and may re-show the drag preview it just tore down. The move should be skipped once `session.active` is false.
triage.cause: no active check after step

claim: swallowClick's guard lets later capture listeners on its own target still receive the click

triage.scenario: Arm guard on a container, add another capture listener on that container; the next click still reaches it and is processed twice
triage.cause: stopPropagation without stopImmediatePropagation

triage.scenario: the user presses toggle A, drags into the gap beside it, then drags back onto A. `reach` returns early on a null item without resetting `current`, so the return to A matches `current` and `enter` is not called. `SweepRun.enter`'s doc says it is "called whenever the item under the pointer changes, so an item swept back over is entered again". Either a gap should clear `current`, or the doc should say that gaps do not count as a change.

claim: A session opened from a window-capture pointerdown listener supersedes itself on the same press
A sweep never reaches the items between its last move and the release point

triage.scenario: a fast flick across a row of toggles where the `pointerup` arrives at a client point past the last `pointermove` (coalesced moves; pointerup is not guaranteed to share the last move's coordinates) → `onEnd` ignores its `ctx` and calls `run.end('commit')` without `travel(end.world)`, so the items between the last move and the release are never entered. The doc promises "an item a fast drag crossed between two moves is entered too". The other drags in this area read the release point: carry `step(e)`s on `onEnd`, handleDrag reports `localOf` of the up event.
triage.cause: release point not traveled on commit

triage.scenario: the header says the list is the union across browsers and desktops and "errs toward listing a chord". But `browserReservedChord({kind:'key', key:' ', mods:{alt:true}}, false)` returns null, and Alt+Space opens the window menu on Windows and many Linux desktops. On a Mac, `{key:' ', mods:{ctrl:true}}` returns null (Ctrl+Space switches the input source), so does `{key:' ', mods:{mod:true, ctrl:true}}` (the emoji and symbols viewer), and so does `{key:'q', mods:{mod:true, shift:true}}` (Log Out). Off a Mac, Ctrl+Shift+Q (quit in Chrome on Linux and Windows) also returns null. A kit default bound to any of these passes the reserved-key check and never fires.
triage.cause: incomplete chord table

A press that only scrolls under a still pointer reports `moved: false` though its point moved

triage.scenario: press a handle and, without moving the pointer, scroll an ancestor with the wheel or a keyboard, then release. `localOf` folds the scroll into the release point, so `onEnd.point` differs from the press's local point, but `moved` is read off client coordinates only (`away` compares `clientX/Y` with the press), so it comes back `false`. A commit-on-end consumer reads that as "a press, not a drag" and throws away an edit whose point did change in the rect's space, the space every other field of `HandleDragEnd` is in.
triage.cause: `moved` measured in client space, `point` in local space

browserReservedChord misses Cmd+Shift+[ / ] when the spec is bound by `code`

triage.scenario: on Apple, `{ kind: 'key', key: '[', code: 'BracketLeft', mods: { mod: true, shift: true } }`. `KeySpec.code` matches the physical key "whatever a held modifier makes it type", so this binding fires on Cmd+Shift+[, which Safari and Chrome take as "previous tab". `keysOf` maps `BracketLeft` only to its unshifted key `[`. The reserved `[` entry requires shift released, and the reserved `{` entry is never compared because `{` is not among the spec's keys. So `browserReservedChord` returns `null` when it should return the "previous and next tab on macOS" chord. The same happens with `BracketRight` / `}`. Digits avoid this only because `345` and `#$%` are both listed.
triage.cause: code-to-key map ignores the shifted character

triage.scenario: with `missedRelease: 'click'`, press, leave the window fast enough that no move inside it crossed the threshold, release outside, and come back: the first move seen has `buttons: 0` and lies far past the threshold. The session asks `missedRelease()` before `onMove` runs, so `activated` is still `false` and the answer is `'end'`. `onEnd` then skips `maybeActivate` (it only runs for `pointerup`) and calls `onClick` for a press that traveled hundreds of pixels. A sticky rect element feeds its own drag back into its coordinate space

triage.scenario: `scrollersOf` starts at `rectEl` itself, so `sticky ??= n` picks `rectEl` when it is `position: sticky`. That includes the default case, where `rectEl` is the HTML handle target. On a stuck axis, `moved()` then reads `box.getBoundingClientRect()` live on every move. If the drag moves that handle (`transform`, `left`/`top`), its rect changes and `localOf` shifts the origin by the same amount. That breaks the contract stated in the doc comment that a handle moving under its own drag must not shift the space its coordinates are reported in. The reported point then drifts or oscillates. The fix is to measure the sticky offset in a way the box's own movement cannot affect, such as its offset against the scroller minus the scroller's scroll at press, or to skip `rectEl` itself.
triage.cause: live rect of the box being measured

claim: The reserved-chord list leaves out chords browsers take and pages cannot override (tab-by-number, back/forward, F5/F12)
pointerSession's `escape` listens at document capture, so window-capture Escape handlers still see the Escape that cancels a drag; thresholdDrag decides the same thing at window capture
A sweep misses an item whose element is reused under a new key

triage.scenario: `reach` enters a new item only when its element differs from the current one **and** its key differs. In a surface that recycles elements (a virtualized grid scrolled mid-sweep, or a row re-keyed after `enter` changes data), the element under the pointer stays the same while `keyOf` now names a different item, so that item is never entered. The doc says `enter` fires "whenever the item under the pointer changes". The key should decide, with the element only breaking ties for keys `keyOf` builds fresh each call.
triage.cause: `&&` where key change alone means a new item

where: packages/routing/src/interactions/handleDrag/handleDrag.ts:120 (stickyScrollerOf), reached from scrollersOf line 98 when `p === root`

claim: swallowNextClick can miss the click a touch release raises, so that click gets through

triage.scenario: the helper assumes the click a release raises is dispatched in the same task as the `pointerup`. For a touch tap, Chrome dispatches the click from the gesture-tap event, a separate input event after `pointerup`/`touchend`; the `setTimeout(…, 0)` that removes the listener can run first, so the drag's release click lands on what the press began on. Mouse is unaffected.
triage.cause: same-task assumption about touch click dispatch

claim: thresholdDrag with `captureAt: 'threshold'` reports a far-travelled release as a click
useHandleDrag ignores page scroll in quirks mode, where the body rather than the root element scrolls the page

triage.scenario: a page in quirks mode (no doctype) scrolls through `document.body`, which is `document.scrollingElement`, and `documentElement.scrollTop` stays 0. The chain ends at `root = documentElement`, so when the page scrolls during a drag, `scrollOf` reads 0 and the handle's local coordinates drift by the scroll distance. The root-held cases at lines 88 and 95 should read `ownerDocument.scrollingElement ?? documentElement`.
triage.cause: reads documentElement instead of scrollingElement

claim: A carry whose release went unseen drops its payload at the next move's point
A sweep hit-tests the press point without the finite-number guard its moves have, so a non-finite press point reaches itemAt

triage.scenario: unruled.md (2026-11-11) rules that a sweep skips a point that is not a finite number, and `travel` does that for moves. `enabled(deps, at)` and `start` pass the press point straight to `itemAt` → `elementFromPoint`, though. A press whose point is `NaN` (a synthesized event with no client coordinates, or a dispatcher mapping that divides by 0) makes `elementFromPoint` throw a TypeError, because its arguments are non-unrestricted doubles. The press point should get the same guard and answer `NotApplicable`. Two paths answer the same question two ways.

claim: `browserReservedChord` misses chords named by a `code` other than `Key*`/`Digit*`
`undoKeyStep` hands the page the undo of a text field inside a closed shadow root

triage.scenario: a page-level keydown handler calls `undoKeyStep(e)` while focus is in an `<input>` inside a closed shadow root. `e.target` names the host, and `isEditableTarget` can only look past a host through `target.shadowRoot`, which is `null` for a closed root, so the field is not seen as editable and Cmd+Z is returned as `'undo'`: the page undoes its own history instead of the field's text. `e.composedPath()[0]` is the focused element in that case only from inside, so the fix is to test the deepest target the event exposes, or `document.activeElement`'s chain.
triage.cause: retargeted event target, closed shadow root

claim: `undoKeyStep` takes a text field inside a shadow root for a non-editable target and hands its Cmd+Z to the page
holdsFixed treats a root element with `filter` or `backdrop-filter` as the containing block for fixed descendants, so a fixed-position rect has the page's scroll subtracted from it

triage.scenario: `<html style="filter: grayscale(1)">` (a common dark-mode or accessibility filter) and a handle whose rect element is `position: fixed`. `holds('fixed', style(html))` is true because `holdsFixed` sees `filter`, so `scrollersOf` stops at `html` and pushes `scrollerOf(root)`. The Filter Effects spec exempts the document root: a filter there does not make a containing block for fixed descendants, so the box stays put in the viewport. A wheel scroll of the page during the drag still shifts `localOf`'s box by the scroll delta, and every `onMove` and `onEnd` point comes back offset by however far the page scrolled. The root should never count as a fixed holder for `filter` or `backdrop-filter`.
triage.cause: root-element exception missing from holdsFixed

claim: A sweep surface whose items sit in its own shadow root never reaches an item

triage.scenario: the surface is a custom element that renders its toggles in its own shadow root. `elementAt(surface, …)` hit-tests in the tree the surface belongs to (the document), not in `surface.shadowRoot`, so it returns the host, which is `surface` itself. The loop `for (; el && el !== surface; …)` exits at once and returns `null`. `enabled` then answers `NotApplicable`, so the sweep never starts. Items in a nested shadow root inside the surface come back retargeted to their host, so `keyOf` sees only the host, and `el.parentElement` stops at shadow-root boundaries either way. The carry and pointer-session code count shadow content as inside its host (`containsComposed`); the sweep does not.
triage.cause: hit test not descending into the surface's shadow root
